name: Liu Huaiyu
current_role: Co-founder and COO, Bambu Lab (Shenzhen consumer 3D-printer maker)
profile: Liu Huaiyu (UESTC class of 1999) was a DJI product manager for DJI Goggles, the digital FPV system and FPV drones before co-founding Bambu Lab in 2020 with fellow DJI engineers led by CEO Tao Ye. Bambu Lab became a global leader in consumer 3D printers (X1, P1, A1, H2 series); he serves as COO.
interesting_fact: Bambu Lab's founding team came out of DJI's core R&D groups and set out to build 3D printers 'to the same standards DJI applied to drones'; its X1 launched via Kickstarter, raising about US$7M.
deep_cut_fact: In January 2026 Liu personally visited his alma mater UESTC to make the first donation under Bambu Lab's 100M-yuan 'Alma Mater Fund', funding a Bambu Lab Scholarship and Teaching Award plus 3D printers for student robotics and model-aircraft clubs.
notes: Low public profile; Bambu Lab's media/influencer channel (contact@bambulab.com, select 'Influencer & Media' category) is the published route. No personal social accounts found.

name: Will Bruey
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Varda Space Industries (El Segundo, CA)
profile: Lancaster, PA-born aerospace engineer (Cornell BS/MS) who spent ~6 years at SpaceX as an avionics lead on Falcon 9 and Dragon, then worked at Merrill Lynch and co-founded VC fund Also Capital. In 2020 he co-founded Varda with Delian Asparouhov to manufacture pharmaceuticals in microgravity and return them to Earth in reentry capsules; he is CEO.
interesting_fact: At SpaceX he was a primary mission-control operator on eight ISS missions and won a 2014 NASA Achievement Award for the video system giving visual feedback during ISS robotics operations.
deep_cut_fact: Starting in high school, Bruey built a Cozy MK IV single-engine experimental aircraft; he also holds a private pilot licence. As a Cornell student he built a power controller for drawing vacuum on Cornell's synchrotron.
notes: Accessible, media-friendly founder; frequent podcast guest. Varda press@varda.com is the published route. Note: Varda is relevant to energy/space-infrastructure angle (hypersonic testbed for DoD).

name: Vitor Cristina
current_role: Co-founder of Tekever (current role not publicly confirmed)
profile: Vítor Cristina co-founded Tekever in 2001 in Lisbon with Instituto Superior Técnico engineering classmates Ricardo Mendes and Pedro Sinogas. Tekever began in software (banking, telecom) and became a maker of AI-enabled surveillance drones (AR3, AR5) used by Ukraine, the UK Home Office and EU agencies, reaching unicorn status (>EUR1.2B) in May 2025.
interesting_fact: Tekever's three founders met in the 1990s as engineering students at Instituto Superior Técnico and started the company straight out of school in 2001.
notes: Very little public information; Observador (2025) reports the founding trio later 'came apart' and only Ricardo Mendes is publicly visible as CEO/chairman. His present shareholding/role is unverified. Route via Tekever media office.

name: Mirko Novakovic
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Dash0 (OpenTelemetry-native observability; HQ New York, founded in Germany)
profile: German serial founder: co-founded IT consultancy codecentric (2005) and APM company Instana, sold to IBM in 2020 for a reported ~$500M. In 2023 he co-founded Dash0, which raised a $110M Series B led by Balderton at a $1B valuation in March 2026 and has acquired Lumigo and Polar Signals. Active angel in 70+ B2B SaaS startups; hosts the Code RED podcast.
interesting_fact: Dash0 went from launch (Nov 2024) to 300+ paying customers in ~10 months and 800+ by 2026; it is OpenTelemetry-native end to end.
deep_cut_fact: When starting Dash0 he set himself a simple rule: hit $1M ARR in year one or shut the company down; the company surpassed it 'by a wide margin'.

public_contacts.value: Code RED (Dash0 podcast hosted by Mirko Novakovic)

notes: Hosts his own podcast (Code RED), so a podcast-swap pitch could resonate. Talks often about AI and data-heavy infra; good fit for data-center angle.
